approvalTitle: Playground requirements (v4 — addresses v3/r3 review; converged)
content:
# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The `playground` spec delivers spec #8 — the final spec in the decomposition: a sandbox section for self-contained "small-web" mini-apps, toys, games, and curiosities. Each item is its own independent thing that doesn't warrant its own repo, CI/CD, or domain. The section provides a gallery/listing of available items, and each item loads in its own space (product.md §7).

This spec builds **on top of** the CSS-isolation foundation that spec #1 (`site-foundation`) already scaffolded and validated. The site-foundation spike concluded outcome **(b) "viable with restrictions"** (`.spec-workflow/specs/site-foundation/spike-results.md`): same-page isolation via an `all: initial` reset container plus an `@layer playground` token re-declaration works, and same-page rendering is **not** cut (the spike-failure/iframe-only contingency is not triggered). Two restrictions are inherited and must be handled by this spec:

- **M1 — typography re-establishment is currently broken.** The unlayered `.playground-container { all: initial }` reset beats the layered `font-family`/`font-size`/`line-height`/`color` re-declarations inside `@layer playground` (unlayered rules win over layered rules on the same selector). Custom properties (the shadcn token path) are unaffected and work correctly. The spike pinned this bug with a broken-state test assertion. This spec must fix it.
- **M2 — shadcn/ui overlay wrappers portal to `document.body`.** No wrapper forwards a `container` prop, so overlays escape the isolation boundary unless explicitly contained. This is a per-item decision, not a global fix.

### Revision notes (v4)

v4 responds to the v3 adversarial review (round 3), which verified every v3 claim against the live repo and judged the document **converged and ready for design** — reversing no conclusions. Three small findings were accepted and folded in:

- **(Would break a green build) The M1 test-fallout list was still one assertion short:** the M1 fix re-declares an unlayered `color: oklch(0.145 0 0)`, which flips `EXPECTED_CONTAINER_COLOR_RGB = [0,0,0]` (`playground-isolation.test.ts:63`) — a constant whose comment (lines 54-62) documents it as encoding the *broken* CanvasText state, and which is read on both the light baseline and the dark "stays light" re-read. v4 generalizes Req 5.3 from "these three edits" to "every assertion/comment encoding the M1 broken state," and explicitly names this constant (flip from `rgb(0,0,0)` to the re-established foreground via `expectLabClose`). It also notes the sibling `EXPECTED_RADIUS = "10px"` stays correct (the fix re-declares `font-size: 16px`, the same value). (Round-3 finding 1.)
- **"Isolation coverage SHALL NOT regress" was slightly overstated:** removing the spike retires its M2 overlay-containment matrix fixture, and neither sample item mounts an overlay, so M2 coverage now lives only as the authoring-doc decision rule. v4 scopes Req 10.2 / Decision #7 honestly — "no regression" applies to the reset/token/leak behaviors; the overlay-containment matrix is intentionally retired. (Round-3 finding 2.)
- **Build-time item-import failure was unstated:** v4 adds one line (Reliability NFR) clarifying that an item whose module fails at build (bad import, type/syntax error) **fails the whole build** by design (fail-loud) — distinct from the runtime error boundary (Req 3.5), so a designer does not assume graceful degradation for a build-broken item. (Round-3 finding 3.)

No other changes; round 3 explicitly confirmed the `<PlaygroundFrame>` extraction, spike removal, themed-gallery token resolution, sitemap production-scoping, and iframe-landing sitemap listing are all sound.

### Revision notes (v3)

v3 responds to the v2 adversarial review (round 2), which verified every v2 claim against the live repo. v2 closed all round-1 findings; round 2 found that two v2 fixes asserted outcomes without mechanizing them, plus smaller gaps. All findings were accepted:

- **(Blocking) The layout refactor needed a concrete mechanism, not a rename (F1/Challenge 2):** v2 said the blanket `(playground)/layout.tsx` "must be refactored" but App Router cannot skip a parent layout per-child, and a `usePathname()` conditional would force the group layout to become a client component (breaking static generation). v3 pins the mechanism: extract the reset into a **shared `<PlaygroundFrame>` component**, **remove** the wrapper from the group layout, and have only the same-page item host wrap with it (Decision #9, Req 5.1). The gallery does **not** move to `(site)` (that would contradict `structure.md`'s assignment of the playground index to `(playground)` and re-import site chrome).
- **(Blocking) Spike-vs-refactor was a hard contradiction, not a soft caveat (F2):** once the reset leaves the group layout, `/spike` loses its `.playground-container` and five isolation tests break. v3 makes a firm choice: **remove the `/spike` fixture and migrate its isolation assertions onto the real same-page sample item** (`site-foundation` deliberately pointed `csp.test.ts` at `/playground`, not `/spike`, so the spike could be removed). (Decision #7, Reqs 7.4, 10.2.)
- **`robots.txt Disallow` was the wrong tool (F3/Challenge 1):** `Disallow: /playground/*/embed` is a Google-only mid-path wildcard, blocks the fetch Google needs to render the indexable landing page and to even read the `noindex`, and is redundant with the per-embed `noindex` already required. v3 **drops the `robots.txt` requirement entirely** and relies on per-embed `robots: { index: false }` + sitemap exclusion — the exact pattern `slash-pages` Decision #3 settled on. (Req 8.4.)
- **Indexability is production-scoped (F3d):** `next.config.ts` already pushes `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` onto `/(.*)` on preview deploys, so "the gallery is indexable" is a **production** statement. v3 scopes all Req 8 indexability rules to production. (Req 8.)
- **Manifest must be server/build-import-safe (F4):** v2's "data + lazy thunks only" invariant protected code-splitting, not the server/build context `sitemap.ts` and `generateStaticParams` need. v3 tightens Req 1.3 to forbid any top-level `"use client"`/React-runtime/browser-global dependency in the manifest module body.
- **Iframe sizing pinned, not deferred (F5):** v3 makes per-item sizing a manifest field available **at launch** (not "a later iteration"), pins a concrete default and a concrete value for the iframe sample, and strengthens the E2E (Req 10.3) to assert the iframe spans the content-column width AND meets its declared height — not merely "≠ 150px." (Reqs 4.4, 7.3, 10.3.)
- **Loading/error reconciled with the dual-mode segment (F6):** v3 states the segment-level `error`/`loading` boundary covers both modes and does not over-promise — `error.tsx` catches render-time throws, not post-hydration event-handler throws. (Req 3.5.)
- **Leak guard narrowed to `:global` (F7):** bare element selectors inside a CSS Module are scoped by the compiler and do not leak; v3 targets the guard at `:global` and non-module global `@import` only. (Reqs 6.2, 10.6.)
- **Embed document a11y (F8):** the host iframe `title` does not cover the framed document; v3 requires each embed document to carry its own `<title>`, `lang`, and a single `<h1>`. (Reqs 4.6, Accessibility NFR.)
- **Sample categories named (F9):** v3 pins the category of each sample at the requirements level (same-page = an interactive canvas/drawing toy; iframe = a viewport-fixed/full-bleed visualization) so Req 7 is verifiable without a design round-trip.

### Revision notes (v2)

v2 responds to the v1 adversarial review (round 1), which verified the document's code claims against the live repo and **read `structure.md`** (which the v1 author had not). The review's central finding was correct: v1 silently relocated the manifest and item modules into `src/app/`, contradicting `structure.md`. All findings were accepted:

- **(Blocking) File locations contradicted `structure.md`:** the manifest belongs at the **project root** `playground/manifest.ts` (sibling to `src/`), and item modules at `playground/[item-name]/` (`index.tsx` + `styles.module.css`), per the `structure.md` tree (lines 83-88), prose (220-239), and the module-boundary import graph (256-271). v2 adopts the steering layout verbatim and aligns the manifest field name to `iframeIsolated` (boolean) as `structure.md` specifies. (Risk 1 / Challenge 1; reworks Reqs 1, 6, Decision #2, NFRs.)
- **Item components are client components, route is the server boundary:** `structure.md:226` says item `index.tsx` "must be a client component." v2 makes the client/server boundary explicit — `[slug]/page.tsx` is the server component (metadata + `generateStaticParams`); it renders the dynamically-imported **client** item — and adds the manifest invariant "data + lazy thunks only, no eager item imports" that keeps the per-item code-split (Req 3.3) real. (Risk 2; Reqs 1, 3.)
- **Embed route must be standalone, not double-wrapped:** `structure.md:277` says embed routes are "complete standalone HTML pages with their own document, layout stack, and provider context — not fragments." v2 requires the `.playground-container` reset to wrap only **item render surfaces**, not the embed route or the gallery, and requires reconciling the existing blanket `(playground)/layout.tsx`. (Risk 3 / Challenge 3; Reqs 2, 4, 5, Decision #9.)
- **Concrete iframe sizing + `dynamicParams = false`:** `all: initial` collapses an iframe to the 300×150 default, so v2 replaces "sensible default size/aspect" with an explicit, assertable sizing rule, and mandates `export const dynamicParams = false` on both dynamic segments so the asserted 404 behavior actually holds (App Router renders unlisted params on demand by default). (Risks 3, 4; Reqs 3.2, 4.4, 4.5.)
- **SEO: list landing routes in the XML sitemap; suppress embed crawling:** v2 reverses v1 Decision #6 for landing routes (they are primary content the product wants discovered) and keeps embed routes out; adds a `robots.txt` `Disallow` for `/playground/*/embed` and requires the iframe-item landing route to carry real title/description text (not a thin empty-iframe shell). (Risk 5 / Challenge 2; Req 8, Decision #6.)
- **Complete the test-fallout list:** v2 expands the M1 test work to the full spike "Test-file fallout" set — invert `INTENDED_PLAYGROUND_FONT_FRAGMENT` (`not.toContain` → `toContain`, assertion at `playground-isolation.test.ts:240`), remove the broken-state/`SPIKE FINDING` comment blocks, and re-audit the `applyDarkMode` helper after the next-themes hydration path (the part most likely to flake). (Finding 6; Reqs 5.3, 10.2.)
- **Cheap leak guard + `data-testid` selection:** v2 adds a one-line CI grep for `:global`/unscoped selectors in item `*.module.css` (the feature's whole safety story is "items don't leak"), and mandates `data-testid` for E2E selection of item content since CSS-Module class hashing differs Turbopack↔Webpack. (Findings 7, 8; Reqs 6, 10.)
- **Loading/error/no-JS states + nested-path CSP assertion + preview decision:** v2 adds an error boundary + loading state for same-page items and a `noscript` notice; extends the CSP-absence E2E to the nested `/playground/[slug]` and `/embed` paths; and explicitly decides text+tags cards at launch (matching `structure.md`'s manifest fields) with an optional preview image deferred. (Findings 9, 10, CSP caveat; Reqs 2, 8, 10.)

### Current state (verified against the codebase and `structure.md`)

These artifacts already exist from `site-foundation` and are **extended in place, not rebuilt**:

- `src/app/(playground)/layout.tsx` — currently wraps **all** `(playground)` children in `<div class="playground-container">`. Because a single App Router segment layout cannot skip wrapping a child, v3 **removes the wrapper from this layout** and re-homes the reset into a shared `<PlaygroundFrame>` component used only by the same-page item host (Decision #9, Req 5.1). The `all: initial` reset CSS itself stays exactly as-is (spike directive); only where it is applied changes.
- `src/styles/playground.css` — unlayered reset block (lines 14-20) + `@layer playground` block (22-77) re-declaring typography and the shadcn token set (mirrored from `tokens.css :root`, light-only by design). The token block is correct; the typography block needs the M1 fix.
- `src/styles/globals.css` — declares `@layer playground;` before `@import "tailwindcss"`, placing the playground layer below Tailwind's layers (so Tailwind utilities win inside the container). This spec does **not** modify this ordering.
- `src/app/(playground)/playground/page.tsx` — a placeholder gallery page (`robots: { index: false }`, "Return home" link). This spec replaces the placeholder body and flips it to indexable + themed.
- `src/app/(playground)/spike/` — the spike fixture (`page.tsx`, `spike-overlays.tsx`). v3 **removes** it and migrates its isolation assertions onto the real same-page sample item (Decision #7); `site-foundation` deliberately pointed `csp.test.ts` at `/playground` (not `/spike`) so the fixture could be removed without breaking the CSP test.
- `next.config.ts` — playground routes **already opt out of CSP** via the negative-lookahead source `/((?!playground(?:/|$)).*)` (`next.config.ts:84`). Verified to exclude `/playground`, `/playground/[slug]`, and `/playground/[slug]/embed`. This spec verifies it and does **not** re-add it. There is no `X-Frame-Options` set by Next or by `next.config.ts`, so same-origin framing of `/embed` is not blocked.
- `e2e/tests/playground-isolation.test.ts` — the isolation regression suite. `INTENDED_PLAYGROUND_FONT_FRAGMENT = "ui-sans-serif"` (line 103) is asserted with `not.toContain` at line 240 (broken-state marker); `HOST_FONT_FAMILY_FRAGMENTS` is the host-leak guard. The spike's "Test-file fallout" note also requires re-auditing `applyDarkMode` after next-themes.
- `e2e/tests/csp.test.ts` — asserts `/playground` serves no CSP header; v2 extends this to the nested item/embed paths (Req 10.5).
- `src/app/sitemap.ts` (XML) lists `/playground`; `src/config/site.ts` `heroCards` links to `/playground`. There is **no** `robots.txt` / `app/robots.ts` in the repo, and v3 does **not** add one (Req 8.4).
- `next.config.ts` already sets `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` on `/(.*)` when `VERCEL_ENV === "preview"`, so **all** indexability statements in this spec are **production-scoped** (preview deliberately noindexes everything). `output` mode is unset (routes are statically prerendered at build via `generateStaticParams`, not a static export).

**`structure.md` is authoritative for layout and module boundaries** (project-root `playground/` directory, `iframeIsolated` manifest flag, client-component items, standalone embed routes, the `(site)`/`(playground)` route-group split). This spec conforms to it; where v1 diverged, v2 was corrected.

### Explicitly in scope at launch

1. A typed **playground manifest** at the project root (`playground/manifest.ts`) as the single source of truth for the gallery, `generateStaticParams`, and per-item dynamic import.
2. The **gallery/index page** at `/playground` — themed, minimally-chromed, rendering one card per manifest entry.
3. A **per-item landing route** `/playground/[slug]` that renders the item inline (same-page) or via an iframe (`iframeIsolated`), driven by the manifest.
4. An **iframe embed route** `/playground/[slug]/embed` — a standalone document for items that need a separate browsing context.
5. The **M1 typography fix** in `playground.css`, with the full spike "Test-file fallout" set applied.
6. The **CSS Modules** convention for same-page item styles, the no-global-CSS authorship constraint, and a cheap CI leak guard.
7. **Two sample items** — one same-page, one iframe — that genuinely exercise the architecture (conflicting colors/fonts/layout), not hello-world divs.
8. Metadata/SEO/indexing for the new routes (production-scoped), including XML-sitemap entries for landing routes and `noindex` + sitemap-exclusion for embeds.
9. Build-time integrity tests (manifest↔route parity), isolation regression updates, and prod-build/Vercel-preview verification.
10. An **authoring doc** for adding a playground item, gated by `scripts/check-authoring-docs.mjs`.

### Explicitly out of scope at launch

- **Playground backends / API routes** (`/api/playground/[item]/`). Items launch client-side only; server capability is evaluated per-item later (tech.md "Server-side convention"). Not built here.
- **pnpm workspace extraction** for dependency-conflicting items (tech.md decision #7 — reserved, not a casual fallback). Conflicting items use iframe isolation instead.
- **Search indexing of playground items.** Pagefind indexes static HTML; dynamic playground content is intentionally not indexed (tech.md "Search scope").
- **Per-item dark/light theming.** Playground items control their own presentation and do not inherit the site theme (product.md §10); the item render surface is pinned light by design. (The gallery, by contrast, **is** themed — see Decision #9.)
- **Visual preview thumbnails for gallery cards** (an optional `preview` field). Deferred (Decision #10); launch cards are text + tags, matching `structure.md`'s manifest fields.
- **Parent↔iframe messaging / decision encoding** for embed items. `structure.md:277` defers this to implementation; no cross-frame protocol ships at launch.

## Alignment with Product Vision

- **Key Feature §7 (Playground):** delivers the gallery + per-item "own space" loading for self-contained experiments.
- **Design principle "Playground extensibility":** the manifest + authoring doc make adding an item a localized, documented change with no site restructuring.
- **Design principle "Progressive complexity":** the main site stays static/pre-rendered; the playground allows per-item architectures (same-page or iframe) without affecting the rest of the site.
- **Target user #4 (Matthew):** the site must be straightforward to extend with new playground items — one manifest entry plus one colocated item folder.

## Shared Definitions (referenced by multiple requirements)

- **Manifest entry** (`PlaygroundItem`): `{ slug, title, description, tags, iframeIsolated, load, frame? }` where `slug` is a URL-safe kebab-case string unique across the manifest; `tags` is a string array; `iframeIsolated` is a boolean; `load` is a **lazy thunk** `() => import("./[slug]")` resolving to the item's client component module; and `frame?` is an optional per-item iframe-sizing hint (e.g. `{ aspectRatio }` or `{ height }`) used only by iframe items (Req 4.4). Field names follow `structure.md`. The manifest module body SHALL be safe to evaluate in a server/build context (Req 1.3). The exact TypeScript shape is finalized in design; this is the contract.
- **Item module**: `playground/[slug]/index.tsx` (a **client component**, per `structure.md:226`) plus colocated `styles.module.css` and any helpers, at the **project root** `playground/` directory.
- **Same-page item** (`iframeIsolated: false`): rendered inline inside `.playground-container` at `/playground/[slug]`, styled with its CSS Module, sharing the Next.js runtime/bundle.
- **iframe item** (`iframeIsolated: true`): the landing route `/playground/[slug]` renders an `<iframe src="/playground/[slug]/embed">`; the item's real content lives at the embed route and runs in its own browsing context.
- **Isolation boundary**: the `.playground-container` element (the `all: initial` reset + `@layer playground` token/typography re-declaration), applied around same-page item render surfaces only.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: Playground manifest (single source of truth)

**User Story:** As the site maintainer, I want a single typed manifest describing every playground item, so that the gallery, static-params generation, and per-item loading never drift out of sync.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the manifest module (`playground/manifest.ts`, project root) is imported THEN it SHALL export a typed array of `PlaygroundItem` entries and an exported `PlaygroundItem` type used by all consumers.
2. The manifest SHALL be the **only** place item metadata is declared; the gallery, both `generateStaticParams` functions, and the `[slug]` loader SHALL all derive from it (no parallel hand-maintained list).
3. The manifest SHALL contain **only** entry data and lazy `() => import(...)` thunks — never an eager top-level import of an item module — so that importing the manifest does not pull item code into unrelated bundles. The manifest module body SHALL additionally be **safe to evaluate in a server/build context**: no top-level `"use client"` directive, no React-runtime, and no browser-global dependency at module scope — because its server/build consumers include `src/app/sitemap.ts` (Req 8.3) and both `generateStaticParams` functions, which would break at build if the manifest pulled client-only code on import.
4. IF two entries share a `slug` THEN this SHALL be caught by the build-time/test integrity check (Req 10.1), never produce a route collision silently.
5. WHEN an entry has `iframeIsolated: true` THEN the same `load` thunk SHALL be consumable by the embed route host (the one item module serves whichever host its mode selects).

### Requirement 2: Gallery / index page

**User Story:** As a visitor, I want a themed gallery of playground items, so that I can browse and open the experiments without leaving the site's look and feel.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a visitor loads `/playground` THEN the system SHALL render one card per manifest entry, each showing the item's title, description, and tags, and linking to `/playground/[slug]`.
2. The gallery SHALL render with the **site theme** (light/dark per the user's selection) and SHALL **not** be wrapped in the `.playground-container` reset — it is a site-section navigation surface, not an isolated item (Decision #9). It SHALL use the shadcn `Card` primitive (cross-spec UI-primitives convention).
3. WHEN the manifest is empty THEN the gallery SHALL render a graceful empty state, not a build error or a blank page.
4. The gallery SHALL provide a visible, keyboard-reachable link back to the main site and a theme toggle (minimal playground chrome).
5. The gallery SHALL be statically generated (server component).

### Requirement 3: Per-item landing route

**User Story:** As a visitor, I want each playground item to open at its own URL, so that items are linkable and load in their own space.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a visitor loads `/playground/[slug]` for a `iframeIsolated: false` entry THEN the system SHALL render the item's client component inline inside `.playground-container`. The `[slug]/page.tsx` route SHALL be the **server** component (metadata + `generateStaticParams`); the dynamic import of the **client** item component defines the client boundary.
2. The system SHALL set `export const dynamicParams = false` on the `[slug]` segment; an unknown slug SHALL therefore 404 (the route MAY additionally call `notFound()` defensively), never render blank or crash.
3. The item component SHALL be loaded via the manifest's lazy `load` thunk so that one item's code is not bundled into unrelated routes (Req 1.3).
4. `generateStaticParams` for `[slug]` SHALL enumerate every manifest slug so all item landing routes are statically generated.
5. The `[slug]` segment SHALL provide a segment-level **loading state** and **error boundary** (`loading.tsx`/`error.tsx` or equivalent) covering **both** render modes (the dynamically-imported same-page item and the iframe-shell render). The loading state is primarily meaningful for the same-page dynamic import; the iframe shell renders fast. This SHALL be understood to catch **render-time** throws and import (thunk) rejections — it does **not** catch post-hydration event-handler throws inside a client item (an item is responsible for its own runtime error handling). The route SHALL also include a `<noscript>` notice since items are interactive and require JavaScript.
6. WHEN a same-page item mounts a shadcn/ui overlay (Dialog, Popover, Tooltip, Select, DropdownMenu) THEN the author SHALL apply the M2 containment decision rule (Decision #5): contain the portal only when the overlay must render against playground-scoped tokens; otherwise accept the `document.body` escape (the default).

### Requirement 4: iframe isolation path

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want an iframe-isolation path for items that need their own browsing context, so that items with viewport-escaping or conflicting global behavior don't break the host page.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a visitor loads `/playground/[slug]` for a `iframeIsolated: true` entry THEN the host route SHALL render an `<iframe>` whose `src` is `/playground/[slug]/embed`, and SHALL also render the item's title and description as real page text (so the landing route is not a thin empty-iframe shell — see Req 8.5).
2. The embed route SHALL live at `src/app/(playground)/playground/[slug]/embed/page.tsx` — **under `/playground/`** so it inherits the permissive (CSP-exempt) playground policy, and SHALL NOT be placed under `/api/` (tech.md "Full isolation").
3. The embed route SHALL render as a **standalone document** (`structure.md:277`): its content is the item's full output and it SHALL **not** be wrapped in the `.playground-container` reset (the reset is for inline same-page items only — Decision #9). It carries no site chrome.
4. The host's `<iframe>` SHALL have explicit, assertable dimensions set via author CSS (since `all: initial` does not apply here — the host is outside the reset — but the iframe still defaults to 300×150 without explicit sizing): width = 100% of the content column, and height from the manifest entry's optional `frame` hint (`aspectRatio` or `height`) **available at launch**, falling back to a concrete documented default (e.g. a 16/10 `aspect-ratio`). The iframe SHALL carry an accessible `title` attribute and be keyboard-reachable.
5. The system SHALL set `export const dynamicParams = false` on the `[slug]/embed` segment, and its `generateStaticParams` SHALL enumerate **only** `iframeIsolated: true` slugs. WHEN a same-page-only slug's `/embed` URL is requested THEN it SHALL cleanly 404, never render a blank/throwing embed.
6. The embed **document** SHALL be accessible in its own right: it SHALL set a `<title>` (the item title), a `lang` attribute, and an appropriate heading structure (a single `<h1>` unless the item's nature dictates otherwise) — the host iframe's `title` attribute does not cover the framed document for screen-reader users who enter the frame.

### Requirement 5: Style-isolation foundation and the M1 typography fix

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want same-page items to render against a known, site-independent baseline, so that the site's styles don't leak in and the item's styles don't leak out.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The system SHALL keep the existing two-part strategy CSS — the unlayered `.playground-container { all: initial; isolation: isolate; … }` reset and the `@layer playground` token re-declaration. The reset CSS SHALL NOT be weakened. Because an App Router segment layout cannot skip wrapping a child, the `.playground-container` wrapper SHALL be **removed from `(playground)/layout.tsx`** and re-homed into a shared **`<PlaygroundFrame>` component** (a server component) that wraps only the same-page item render surface inside `[slug]/page.tsx` (for `iframeIsolated: false`). The gallery and the embed route therefore render outside the reset. The gallery SHALL NOT be moved to `(site)` (that would contradict `structure.md`'s assignment of the playground index to `(playground)` and re-import site chrome).
2. The system SHALL fix M1 so the intended `ui-sans-serif, system-ui, …` font stack (and `font-size`/`line-height`/`color`) actually applies inside `.playground-container` — via the spike's preferred approach (a second **unlayered** rule on `.playground-container`, declared after the reset). The shadcn token re-declarations SHALL remain layered (so Tailwind utilities still win).
3. WHEN M1 is fixed THEN the system SHALL update **every assertion and comment in `e2e/tests/playground-isolation.test.ts` that encodes the M1 broken state**, not just one — specifically at least: (a) invert `INTENDED_PLAYGROUND_FONT_FRAGMENT` from `not.toContain` (assertion at line 240) to `toContain`; (b) flip `EXPECTED_CONTAINER_COLOR_RGB` (line 63, currently `[0,0,0]` documenting the broken CanvasText state, read on both the light baseline and the dark "stays light" re-read) to the re-established foreground value, asserted via `expectLabClose` (the fixed `color` is a `lab()`/`oklch()` value, not `rgb`); (c) remove the "broken-state marker"/`SPIKE FINDING` comment blocks; (d) re-audit the `applyDarkMode` helper for the next-themes hydration path per `spike-summary.txt:365-398`. Note: `EXPECTED_RADIUS = "10px"` stays correct (the fix re-declares `font-size: 16px`, the same value `var(--radius)` resolves against) — do not over-correct it.
4. WHEN the host site is in dark mode AND a same-page item is open THEN the item SHALL continue to render against the playground's light tokens (the item surface does not inherit the site theme) — preserving the spike's verified behavior.
5. The host-leak guard (`HOST_FONT_FAMILY_FRAGMENTS`, asserting site-only fonts do NOT appear inside the container) SHALL remain in place and continue to pass.

### Requirement 6: CSS Modules scoping for same-page items

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want same-page item styles scoped so multiple items can't collide or leak, so that adding an item is safe.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a same-page item needs styles THEN it SHALL author them in a colocated CSS Module (`playground/[slug]/styles.module.css`) so class names are hashed and collision-free.
2. Playground item styles SHALL NOT write **global** CSS rules — specifically `:global(...)` blocks or `@import` of a non-module global stylesheet, which are the only constructs that escape CSS-Module scoping (a bare element selector like `div { … }` inside a module **is** scoped by the compiler and is permitted). This is documented in the authoring doc (Req 11) AND guarded by a cheap CI check targeting `:global`/global `@import` (Req 10.6); no full custom linter is required.
3. Item modules SHALL live at the project-root `playground/[slug]/` directory and use `@/` aliases for `src/` imports and relative imports within their own directory (`structure.md` import rules); items SHALL NOT import from `src/app/`, `src/components/shared/`, or `src/components/layout/`.

### Requirement 7: Sample items (one per isolation mode)

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want one real sample item in each isolation mode shipped at launch, so that the architecture is proven end-to-end and there is a copyable template.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The launch set SHALL include at least one **same-page** item (`iframeIsolated: false`) and one **iframe** item (`iframeIsolated: true`), both functional and interactive.
2. The same-page sample SHALL be an **interactive canvas/drawing toy** (category pinned here; design picks the exact item) that sets colors, fonts, and layout properties which would visibly conflict with the main site theme (proving the reset + CSS Modules genuinely isolate), per the decomposition's "trivial hello-world divs don't exercise the isolation architecture." It SHALL carry the `data-testid` hooks needed to host the migrated isolation-regression assertions (Req 10.2).
3. The iframe sample SHALL be a **viewport-fixed / full-bleed visualization** (category pinned here) that exercises a concrete pattern justifying iframe isolation — `position: fixed`/viewport units or document-level styling that would escape the same-page boundary (tech.md's iframe-required examples). Its manifest entry SHALL declare a concrete `frame` sizing hint (Req 4.4) sufficient for its content (a fixed default that clips viewport-escaping content is not acceptable for this sample).
4. WHEN either sample is opened from the gallery THEN it SHALL render correctly with no visual leakage from or into the surrounding context, asserted via `data-testid` selectors (Req 10.3).

### Requirement 8: Metadata, SEO, and indexing

**User Story:** As Matthew, I want the playground routes titled, discoverable, and indexed appropriately, so that the section and its items are found but iframe internals aren't surfaced as standalone pages.

> All indexability criteria below are **production-scoped**: on Vercel preview deploys, `next.config.ts` already applies `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` to every route, which intentionally overrides the per-page `index` settings here.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. In production, the gallery `/playground` SHALL be **indexable** (flip the placeholder's `robots: { index: false }`) and SHALL export `generateMetadata()` with the site title template and default OG image (cross-spec metadata convention). It remains in the XML sitemap.
2. Each `/playground/[slug]` landing route SHALL export per-item metadata (title/description from the manifest) and SHALL be indexable in production.
3. The system SHALL add the `/playground/[slug]` landing routes to the XML sitemap (`src/app/sitemap.ts`) by deriving them from the (server/build-import-safe, Req 1.3) manifest (reversing v1 Decision #6 — items are primary content the product wants discovered).
4. Each `/playground/[slug]/embed` route SHALL be `robots: { index: false }` and SHALL NOT appear in the XML sitemap. **No `robots.txt` `Disallow` is added**: `noindex` is the correct tool ("fetchable but not separately indexed"), whereas `Disallow` would block the crawl Google needs to render the indexable landing page that frames the embed and to even read the `noindex`; this also matches `slash-pages` Decision #3 (noindex → sitemap exclusion, no robots.txt). The system SHALL NOT advertise any `noindex` route in the XML sitemap.
5. For `iframeIsolated` items, the landing route's indexable HTML SHALL include the item's title and description as real text (Req 4.1) so the indexed page is not thin/empty-shell content while its real content sits at the `noindex` embed URL.

### Requirement 9: Security and CSP

**User Story:** As Matthew, I want the playground's relaxed CSP scoped to playground routes only, so that the rest of the site keeps its protective CSP.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The system SHALL rely on the **existing** route-scoped CSP opt-out for `/playground/*` in `next.config.ts` (negative-lookahead source `/((?!playground(?:/|$)).*)`); this spec SHALL NOT re-add or duplicate that rule, and SHALL NOT relax CSP for any non-playground route.
2. WHEN the iframe host (`/playground/[slug]`) embeds `/playground/[slug]/embed` THEN the same-origin embed SHALL load without a CSP/framing error (both routes are CSP-exempt; no `X-Frame-Options` is set — verified).
3. Playground items SHALL have no authentication, no stored user data, and no sensitive operations at launch (tech.md acceptance rationale). The relaxed CSP **permits** external resources and inline code; this is acceptable only because items are first-party. This is an authorship constraint, not an enforced boundary, and SHALL be stated as such in the authoring doc (Req 11).
4. External `target="_blank"` links inside items SHALL use `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

### Requirement 10: Build-time integrity and test coverage

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want tests that fail loudly when the playground wiring regresses, so that adding or renaming items can't silently break routing or isolation.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The system SHALL have a test asserting manifest↔route integrity: every manifest slug is unique; every slug resolves to a `/playground/[slug]` route; every `iframeIsolated: true` slug resolves to an embed route and every `iframeIsolated: false` slug does not.
2. The system SHALL keep the isolation regression suite (`e2e/tests/playground-isolation.test.ts`) green by **re-pointing its container/descendant assertions from the removed `/spike` fixture onto the real same-page sample item** (Req 7.2), and SHALL apply the full M1 "Test-file fallout" set (Req 5.3) and retain the host-leak guard (Req 5.5). Coverage of the **reset / token re-declaration / typography / leak behaviors** SHALL NOT regress relative to the spike fixture. The spike's **M2 overlay-containment matrix** fixture is **intentionally retired** (neither sample mounts an overlay); M2 is now an authoring-doc decision rule (Decision #5, Req 3.6), not a fixtured regression test — this is a deliberate scope reduction, not a coverage bug.
3. The system SHALL include an E2E that opens each sample item from the gallery and asserts it renders — same-page item content visible inside the `.playground-container`; the iframe item's `<iframe>` present, its embed document loaded, AND its rendered box spanning the content-column width and meeting its declared `frame` height/aspect (not merely "≠ the 150px collapse default") — selecting by `data-testid` (never by hashed CSS-Module class, which differs Turbopack↔Webpack).
4. WHEN the isolation suite is run THEN it SHALL run against a **production build** (Webpack), since `@layer` ordering and CSS Modules hashing can differ between Turbopack (dev) and Webpack (prod); item isolation SHALL additionally be verified on a Vercel preview deploy before merge.
5. The E2E suite SHALL assert that `/playground`, `/playground/[slug]`, AND `/playground/[slug]/embed` serve **no** `Content-Security-Policy` header (extending the existing `csp.test.ts`, which currently only checks `/playground`), confirming the route-scope opt-out holds for the nested paths where a future regex refactor would regress.
6. The system SHALL add a cheap CI guard that fails if any `playground/**/*.module.css` contains a `:global(...)` block or an `@import` of a non-module global stylesheet (Req 6.2) — a grep-level check targeting only the constructs that genuinely escape module scope, not bare element selectors (which are scoped and permitted).

### Requirement 11: Authoring documentation

**User Story:** As the maintainer (and future me), I want a documented procedure for adding a playground item, so that extending the section is a localized, repeatable change.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The system SHALL add `docs/playground-authoring.md` documenting: where item modules live (`playground/[slug]/index.tsx` client component + `styles.module.css`), how to add a manifest entry, how to pick an isolation mode (the tech.md "when in doubt, use iframe" rule and the patterns that require iframe), the CSS Modules + no-global-CSS constraint, the `@/`-alias / no-`src/app`-import rule, and the M2 overlay-containment decision rule.
2. The authoring doc SHALL be gated by the existing `scripts/check-authoring-docs.mjs` (added to its doc-list, the same drift protection the `slash-pages` and `contributions-and-resources` docs use); the script's self-test (`scripts/check-authoring-docs.test.mjs`) SHALL be updated if the doc-list change affects it.
3. The authoring doc SHALL state the launch constraints: client-side only, no playground backend, first-party items only, and that the relaxed CSP is an authorship privilege not an enforced sandbox.

## Decisions (resolved during requirements authoring)

1. **Same-page isolation is viable and used** — per the spec-1 spike outcome (b). The iframe-only contingency is **not** triggered; both isolation modes ship. (Source: `spike-results.md`.)
2. **Manifest is code at the project root, not Velite, not under `src/app/`** — playground items are code modules with per-item architecture, so the single source of truth is a typed `playground/manifest.ts` at the **project root** (sibling to `src/`), with item modules at `playground/[slug]/`, exactly per `structure.md` (tree 83-88, prose 220-239, import graph 256-271). The manifest flag is `iframeIsolated` (boolean) per `structure.md`. (Reverses v1's `src/app/(playground)/playground/manifest.ts` placement; addresses v1 Risk 1 / Challenge 1.)
3. **Every item has a `/playground/[slug]` landing route** — same-page items render inline there; iframe items render an `<iframe>` to `/playground/[slug]/embed` there. One consistent, linkable URL per item; the embed route stays under `/playground/` for the CSP exemption.
4. **M1 fixed via unlayered typography re-establishment** (spike's preferred option) — keeps the token path layered (Tailwind utilities win) while giving typography the specificity it needs. The full spike "Test-file fallout" set lands with it (Req 5.3). (Source: `spike-results.md` M1.)
5. **M2 handled per-item, default to `document.body` escape** — contain overlay portals only when the overlay must render against playground-scoped tokens. Captured as an authoring rule, not a global mechanism. (Source: `spike-results.md` M2.)
6. **XML sitemap lists the gallery AND landing routes; embed routes are `noindex` + sitemap-excluded (no `robots.txt`)** — items are primary content destinations the product wants discovered (product.md §7, target user #3), and feeding the manifest to `sitemap.ts` is trivial given its existing shape. Embed routes use `robots: { index: false }` + sitemap exclusion only; a `robots.txt Disallow` is **not** added — `Disallow` is non-portable for the mid-path-wildcard pattern, blocks the crawl Google needs to render the framing landing page, and is redundant with `noindex`. This matches `slash-pages` Decision #3. (Reverses v1 Decision #6 for landing routes; v2/v3 refine the embed crawl handling — addresses v1 Risk 5 and v2 F3.)
7. **Spike fixture is removed; its assertions migrate to the same-page sample** — once the layout refactor (Decision #9) moves the reset out of the group layout, `/spike` would lose its `.playground-container` and break five tests. Rather than make the spike self-wrap (busywork once a real sample exists), v3 removes `src/app/(playground)/spike/` and re-points the isolation-regression assertions onto the same-page sample item, which carries equivalent `data-testid` hooks (Req 7.2, 10.2). `site-foundation` already pointed `csp.test.ts` at `/playground` so the fixture could be removed cleanly. The spike's M2 overlay-containment matrix is intentionally retired with it (M2 becomes an authoring rule, not a fixtured test — Req 10.2). (Firm choice replacing v2's optional caveat; addresses v2 F2 and v3 round-3 finding 2.)
8. **CSP opt-out is reused, not rebuilt** — site-foundation already scoped CSP off for `/playground/*`; this spec verifies it (Req 9, Req 10.5) and does not touch the rule.
9. **The gallery is themed and outside the reset; only same-page item surfaces are isolated; embeds are standalone** — `structure.md` assigns the playground index to `(playground)`, and its providers (theme/fonts) come from the shared root layout, so the gallery can be themed without site chrome. Pinning the *gallery* (a navigation surface) to light-only would give dark-mode visitors a jarring forced-light landing — so the `.playground-container` reset is **removed from `(playground)/layout.tsx`** and re-homed into a shared `<PlaygroundFrame>` server component that wraps only same-page item surfaces. This is the only restructuring consistent with `structure.md` (the alternative — moving the gallery to `(site)` — would re-import site chrome the gallery omits; and a `usePathname()` conditional in the layout would force it to become a client component, breaking static generation). Embed routes are standalone documents (`structure.md:277`), also outside the reset. (Addresses v1 Risk 3 / Challenge 3 and v2 F1/F2; product.md §10 pins *items*, not the gallery, to no-theme.)
10. **Text+tags gallery cards at launch; preview image deferred** — `structure.md`'s manifest fields are slug/title/description/tags/`iframeIsolated` (no image). Playground items are code, not photo-worthy, so launch cards are text + tags; an optional `preview` field is a clean future addition. Stated explicitly rather than omitted. (Addresses v1 Finding 10.)

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- **Single Responsibility**: `playground/manifest.ts` holds item metadata + lazy thunks (data only); `[slug]/page.tsx` owns same-page-vs-iframe routing + metadata + `dynamicParams`; `[slug]/embed/page.tsx` owns the standalone embed render; each `playground/[slug]/index.tsx` owns one item's behavior + its CSS Module; `playground.css` + the shared `<PlaygroundFrame>` component own the isolation boundary (the group layout no longer applies it — Decision #9).
- **Modular Design**: each playground item is self-contained in its own project-root `playground/[slug]/` folder; adding one touches the manifest plus the item folder and nothing else.
- **Dependency Management**: items share the single dependency tree (tech.md decision #7); items whose dependencies conflict use iframe isolation rather than workspace extraction. Items import only from `src/lib/`, `src/components/ui/`, and their own directory (`structure.md` boundary).
- **Clear Interfaces**: the `PlaygroundItem` type is exported from `manifest.ts` and is the contract used by the gallery, both route hosts, both `generateStaticParams`, and `sitemap.ts`.

### Performance

- The gallery and item landing routes are statically generated; item code loads via lazy manifest thunks so it isn't bundled into unrelated routes (Req 1.3).
- **Lighthouse performance target: 90+** on the gallery, verified at launch (cross-spec performance-baseline convention). Individual interactive items are exempt from the strict budget where their own architecture dictates (product.md progressive-complexity), but SHALL not regress the gallery.

### Security

- Relaxed CSP is scoped to `/playground/*` only; the rest of the site keeps its protective CSP unchanged.
- Items are first-party, client-side, with no auth or stored data at launch; the CSP relaxation is an authorship privilege, not an enforced sandbox (Req 9.3).
- External `target="_blank"` links inside items SHALL use `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

### Reliability

- An unknown `[slug]` SHALL 404 via `dynamicParams = false` (Req 3.2), never crash or render blank; a same-page slug's `/embed` SHALL 404 (Req 4.5).
- A slow or throwing same-page item SHALL be caught by the route's loading state + error boundary (Req 3.5), not crash the route. This covers **runtime** render-throws and thunk rejections; an item whose module fails at **build** (bad import, type/syntax error) SHALL fail the whole `next build` by design (fail-loud — a broken item does not ship), which is distinct from and not masked by the runtime error boundary.
- An empty manifest SHALL produce a graceful empty gallery, not a build error.
- Manifest↔route integrity, isolation regressions, and the CSS leak guard SHALL fail CI (Req 10).

### Usability

- The gallery renders correctly in both themes (it is themed); same-page items render correctly with WCAG 2.1 AA contrast within the playground's light token set.
- iframes carry an accessible `title`, non-collapsed dimensions, and are keyboard-reachable.
- The gallery provides a visible path back to the main site and a theme toggle.

### Accessibility

- The gallery uses semantic landmarks and a single `<h1>`; item cards use accessible link names.
- Each item landing route has a single `<h1>` (the item title) or an item-appropriate heading structure.
- Each **embed document** (loaded standalone in its iframe) carries its own `<title>`, `lang`, and an appropriate heading — the host iframe `title` attribute does not cover the framed document (Req 4.6).
- WCAG 2.1 AA violations on the new playground pages are blocking issues (cross-spec accessibility convention); items that intentionally subvert conventions (games/toys) document any deviations in the authoring doc.

### Maintainability

- Adding a playground item is: one manifest entry + one project-root `playground/[slug]/` folder (+ `iframeIsolated` flag) — no site restructuring.
- The authoring doc (Req 11) is the single source of authoring truth and is drift-gated by `scripts/check-authoring-docs.mjs`.
- Cross-document citations use stable symbol/file references rather than volatile line numbers where practical.
